question: Differentiate $$f(x)=\sin\left(\cos(x^2)\right)$$ with respect to $x$.
explanation:
Successive inner functions
Let $u=x^2$, $v=\cos u$ and $f=\sin v$.
Individual derivatives
$$\frac{du}{dx}=2x,\qquad \frac{dv}{du}=-\sin u,\qquad \frac{df}{dv}=\cos v$$
Repeated application of the chain rule
$$\frac{df}{dx}=\frac{df}{dv}\frac{dv}{du}\frac{du}{dx}$$
$$\frac{df}{dx}=\cos(\cos x^2)(-\sin x^2)(2x)$$
Therefore, $$f'(x)=-2x\sin(x^2)\cos(\cos(x^2))$$
